chunks: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, both together from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from a sheikh from our companions known as Abu al-Hasan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and High, created a white rooster, its neck is beneath the Throne, and its feet are at the edges of the seventh earth. It has a wing in the East and a wing in the West. The roosters do not crow until it crows. So whenever it crows, it flaps its wings, then says: 'Glory be to Allah! Glory be to Allah the Magnificent, Who does not resemble anything.' He said: So Allah, Blessed and High, answers it, saying: 'He would not swear by Me falsely, the one who recognizes what you are saying.'

key_terms.تُخُومِ الْأَرْضِ السَّابِعَةِ: The edges of the seventh earth

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the cosmic rooster in Shia cosmology?
ai.summary: In the context of validating oaths, this hadith from Al-Kafi introduces a cosmic rooster whose preeminent crowing serves as a divine witness to truthfulness, reinforcing the gravity of swearing by Allah. The narrative highlights the metaphysical hierarchy where this creature's glorification elicits a direct response from Allah, affirming that those who know the reality of His name do not lie. This imagery underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the tangible spiritual presence of divine attributes in the unseen world.
